title: Wall Street Bounces Back as Housing Data Impresses and Treasury Yields Pull Back
intro:
US Stocks Rebound as Yields and Oil Retreat
U.S. equities rebounded sharply on Thursday, recovering from the previous session's Fed-driven selloff as Treasury yields eased and crude oil prices extended their decline. The rally followed the Federal Reserve's first interest rate hike in more than three years, with investors taking comfort from resilient economic data and easing inflation concerns.

The S&P 500 rose 1.14% to 7,637.76, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.69% to 26,418.30 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.61% to 51,778.04. The move snapped a three-session losing streak and marked the strongest daily advance in roughly six weeks.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield fell back to 4.95% after briefly moving above 5% earlier in the week, while oil prices retreated from recent highs, helping improve overall market sentiment.
Economic data also supported risk assets. Initial jobless claims declined, while both single-family housing starts and pending home sales increased, reinforcing confidence in the resilience of the U.S. economy.

Technology and Semiconductors Lead the Rally
Technology stocks led the advance, climbing more than 2.2%, while semiconductor shares surged over 4%. Nine of the eleven major S&P 500 sectors finished in positive territory.
Intel (INTC) jumped 7.7% amid broad chip-sector strength and reports of discussions involving SK Hynix.
Marvell Technology (MRVL) gained 4.8% as investors continued to favor AI and data infrastructure-related names.


Healthcare Sector
Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical (RARE) surged 12.6% after receiving FDA approval for its gene therapy targeting a rare pediatric neurological disorder.
Industrial and Infrastructure Stocks
Generac Holdings (GNRC) soared 18.7% after announcing a long-term agreement with Amazon (AMZN) to supply up to $8 billion worth of backup generators for data centers. The contract includes approximately $2.4 billion in initial deliveries scheduled for 2027 and 2028.

Financial Technology and Digital Assets
Securitize (SECZ) gained roughly 15% after the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission granted a five-year exemption allowing tokenized U.S. stock trading, a milestone for blockchain-based financial infrastructure.

Consumer and Clean Energy Stocks
Fluence Energy (FLNC) fell 15.4% after lowering its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $2.4 billion from as much as $3.1 billion due to manufacturing delays at its Houston facility.
AutoNation (AN) dropped 10.5% after management indicated that customers were becoming increasingly selective, raising concerns about consumer spending trends.

Housing Sector
Homebuilders outperformed following stronger-than-expected housing data.
Lennar (LEN) gained 1.7% during the regular session before reporting third-quarter results after the market close. The company posted earnings of $1.23 per share versus expectations of $1.32, while revenue came in at $8.05 billion compared with the $8.39 billion consensus estimate.

Central Banks in Focus
The Federal Reserve remained the key market driver after delivering its first rate hike in more than three years. Investors continue to evaluate whether additional tightening will be necessary in the months ahead.
Meanwhile, the Bank of Japan raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 1.25%, marking the highest level since 1995. Policymakers cited persistent inflation pressures and the risk that elevated energy costs could eventually push inflation above target.
Japan's annual inflation rate remained at 1.9% in August, while core inflation eased to 1.7%, remaining below the Bank of Japan's 2% target.

Currency Markets
The offshore Chinese yuan strengthened to around 6.69 per U.S. dollar, its strongest level since July 2022. The move followed another stronger daily fixing from the People's Bank of China and came ahead of scheduled meetings between senior U.S. and Chinese officials.
The U.S. Dollar Index remained near 100.2, close to seven-week highs, as investors assessed the Federal Reserve's outlook and the possibility of further policy tightening.

Oil Market
Crude oil prices declined for a third consecutive session as concerns over Middle East supply disruptions eased.
Saudi Arabia continued efforts to restore capacity on its East-West pipeline, while reports suggested increased diplomatic engagement aimed at reducing regional tensions. The easing supply concerns helped reduce inflation fears and contributed to the decline in Treasury yields.

Gold Market
Gold traded near $4,350 per ounce after rallying nearly 2% in the previous session.
The precious metal benefited from lower oil prices, softer inflation expectations, and falling bond yields. Investors also continued to assess the implications of the Federal Reserve's latest policy decision and the possibility of further tightening later this year.

Market Outlook
Investors now turn their attention to upcoming U.S. economic data releases and additional comments from Federal Reserve officials.
With Treasury yields pulling back from recent highs, oil prices correcting lower, and economic indicators remaining resilient, markets will be watching closely to determine whether the latest rebound represents the start of a more sustainable recovery or simply a relief rally within a higher-rate environment.
